items.title: Spool: Low-Latency Streaming Inference for Hybrid Vision-Language Models
items.summary: Applications such as visual accessibility agents and robotics require answering questions about recent video content promptly, over a bounded window of past frames (e.g., the last two minutes). Hybrid vision-language models (VLMs), which interleave attention with linear recurrent layers such as Gated DeltaNet (GDN), are attractive for this setting, but maintaining a sliding window is expensive. The reason is that recurrent layers combine all past frames into a shared state, so expiring old frames normally requires re-running the entire window through the model. We observe that the recurrent update is affine in the state with input-dependent coefficients, so the effect of each frame can be captured as a transformation that composes associatively. We present Spool, a training-free framework that caches per-frame state transformations and composes them efficiently as the window advances, removing expired frames from each recurrent layer's state without replaying frames through the backbone. Removal is exact within each layer; as with key-value eviction in attention, expired frames can retain residual influence through the cached inputs computed by earlier layers. We design a dedicated data structure and GPU kernels to achieve low caching and composition overhead. Across five open-source hybrid VLMs and four video reasoning benchmarks, Spool achieves the lowest p95 time-to-first-token in all 20 model-benchmark tests, reducing it by a geometric mean of $6.6\times$ over the faster of two recent vLLM baselines, while improving accuracy by 2.3 percentage points on average.

items.title: Runtime Verification of Multiple Natural Language Criteria for Agent Governance
items.summary: AI agents are governed by hundreds of natural language criteria, yet existing verifiers cannot efficiently evaluate an agent's output against a large set of such criteria and report which are satisfied, violated, or inapplicable. We introduce the VFM, a tree-attention verifier that encodes the shared context and target text, and scores N natural language criteria in parallel, returning independent per-criterion ternary verdicts. The VFM is pretrained on CriteriaBank, a corpus of 394K (context, target, criterion, verdict) tuples spanning over 321K distinct criterion strings. A finetuned VFM-4B outperforms GPT-5.4 on a synthetic governance benchmark. On the DynaBench multi-criterion benchmark, it outperforms DynaGuard-4B on trace-level failure detection, and its per-criterion verdicts localize the violated rule and support focused escalation to a larger chain-of-thought judge. We show that CriteriaBank pretraining improves cross-domain transfer, particularly in the low-data regime, while matching a strong direct-finetuning control at full data. On a single H100, VFM-4B evaluates 1,000 criteria against a 4K-token context in under 2s at <11 GB VRAM, making it suitable for runtime verification.

items.title: ForecastGym: A Live, Controlled, and Replayable Benchmark for Forecasting Agents
items.summary: Agents built on large language models (LLMs) increasingly forecast real-world events by searching the Web and reasoning over what they find. How well such an agent forecasts depends on both the retrieved evidence and the model, making control over that evidence essential for evaluation. Live evaluations can mix retrieval with reasoning when each system searches on its own, while retrospective search can leak later information through date filters or today's ranking of historical pages. Comparing models, search sources, and memory strategies requires both fixed evidence and a record of how it evolved before resolution. We introduce ForecastGym, which records what four commercial web search APIs return for open prediction-market questions every two days and replays this frozen evidence offline once outcomes are known, comparing models, memory, and captured search sources under a fixed evidence-acquisition policy. Its first release covers 150 questions, 614 evidence states, one per question and collection time, and 131k search results. Rerunning the same queries after settlement returns results that all but state the outcome for up to 92% of the questions, despite the tested date filters. On the frozen evidence, all tested LLMs trail the market in forecasting accuracy. Our diagnostic analysis suggests that missed public information contributes more to the gap in high-gap states than misreading does. Switching the search API changes a model's Brier score by up to 0.043, more than the spread across models, while persistent notes score similarly to rereading all evidence at half the input tokens. The evidence a forecaster sees can matter as much as the model that reads it.

items.content_excerpt: Last week we shipped 7 launches across models, agent infrastructure, benchmarks, and science: two Gemini 4 models, our first Decision Model & API, self-hosted agent sandboxes, a new visual knowledge benchmark, and new robotics and genomics models. Gemini 4 Carbon , available as gemini-4-carbon , is our strongest reasoning model for repository-scale engineering, formal proofs, and cybersecurity defense. Gemini 4 Hydrogen , available as gemini-4-hydrogen , is our recommended upgrade from Gemini 3.8 Flash for everyday coding and fast agentic workflows. Hydrogen and Carbon share the same 1M unified context window, long decode architecture, and Interactions API schema. Pick the model that matches your reasoning depth, latency, and cost target: You can also pair Carbon and Hydrogen. Use Carbon to plan and orchestrate and Hydrogen to execute. The Gemini Decisions API , powered by Gemini Decision 1 , evaluates text, images, video, PDFs , or audio across up to 256K tokens against up to 1,000 isolated questions with 0 output tokens billed. Three question types return calibrated probabilities and a confidence score: noul for binary yes/no checks, choice across 2 to 255 discrete keys, and score for ordered rubrics. Pass media via base64, HTTPS URLs, or the Files API , and test rubrics in the Gemini Decisions Playground . Here's a runnable check over our sample WAV file: Gemini Managed Agents now supports self-hosted environments . We run model inference and the agent loop on Google infrastructure while bash commands and file edits execute inside your compute. Your worker connects over outbound HTTPS with a scoped key and zero inbound firewall ports. In production, you can deploy across Modal, E2B, Cloudflare, Daytona, Fly.io , Vercel, or Cloud Run using our self-hosted provider manifests . To test it end to end on your own machine, install our open-source gemini-api CLI from the CLI guide and run this single script. It creates a self-hosted environment via REST, spawns a local worker confined to ./sandbox , runs the managed agent locally, and cleans up the environment when finished. Local mode executes bash directly on your host unless you run inside a container or pass --disable-bash : We partnered with Artificial Analysis to release the Multimodal Knowledge Agent benchmark , evaluating 200 multi-step tasks across 10 verticals built around load-bearing visuals: CAD blueprints, RF schematics, GIS maps, gel plates, and charts. items.content_excerpt: Last week we announced our series C and introduced the new LangSmith Agent Platform : a single place to build, run, improve, and govern every agent. With this, agents are now the core object across LangSmith, connecting fragmented workflows for developers and enabling platform teams to manage agents across the business. In this post, we discuss why we reorganized the product, how the agent model works, what it unlocks, and where we're taking it next. 2026 brought a step change in agent adoption as new harnesses , models, and engineering approaches made it possible to build agents that can reliably perform complex, high value work . Companies now run many agents across the business: engineering uses coding agents, product is building customer-facing agents, and teams across the organization have various internal productivity agents. These agents are built with different frameworks, hosted on various runtimes, and use a variety of tools and models. Engineers work across disconnected surfaces. Tracing , monitoring , and deployments all live in different places. This requires frequent context switching, and in practice results in teams skipping difficult but important steps like building the evals. AI Platform teams have difficulty answering basic governance questions. Which agents exist, and who owns each of them? What do they cost, and how are they performing? When costs spike, there is often no obvious person to ask what happened. We wanted to make it simple for teams to manage the entire agent development lifecycle from one place, using any stack, with ownership and governance across all of it. LangSmith supports the entire agent development lifecycle: build, run, improve, and govern. Now, we've connected the entire process through a unique agent record. When you open an agent record, its traces, evals, Agent Server, and Engine issues are accessible with one click, so you don’t need to navigate multiple surfaces to find them. Each agent’s local, dev, staging, and production environments sit under the same agent ID, so comparing performance after making changes is simple. LangSmith is composable, so you can choose the parts you need. If you already run your agent on another platform, you can connect it to LangSmith to improve and govern it without changing any other workflows. items.title: vllm v0.34.0
items.summary:
v0.34.0

1,061 commits from 412 contributors (120 new). Thank you!

TL;DR

  • 10 new models (Mistral Large 4, MiniMax-M3.1-Flash, Nemotron-3.5-Transcribe, and more!)
  • Extensible KV cache is on by default: vLLM sizes the KV cache from memory actually free after warmup, so most models get a bigger cache and more throughput.
  • Model Runner V1 is gone. Model Runner V2 is now the only GPU runner.
  • Big speedups on Blackwell and MI355X: up to 1.95× decode (Step5 on GB200), 1.6× throughput (GLM-5.3-Flash), 1.24–1.40× faster long-prompt TTFT (GLM-5.3).
  • Upgrade check: default block size is now 64, ROCm 7.2 images are gone, and huggingface_hub >= 2.0.0 is required. See Before you upgrade.

Before you upgrade

Important

These changes can break existing setups.

Change What to do PR

Default --block-size is 64 (was 16) Pass --block-size 16 to keep the old behavior. ROCm paged attention still uses 16. #63231
Extensible KV cache on by default; gpu_memory_utilization defaults to 1.0 To keep the old sizing, pass --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 or --no-enable-extensible-kv-cache. #56492
ROCm 7.2 artifacts dropped Use the ROCm 10.0 wheels and images. -rocm72 is no longer published. #61939

QuTLASS / fp_quant removed fp_quant checkpoints no longer load. #65230

New models

Model Notes PR

MiniMax-M3.1-Flash Blackwell NVFP4 and ROCm kernels, DSpark draft #64111

Baidu Unlimited-OCR-2 DASH sparse attention #64016
Liquid AI LFM3, LFM3-VL, LFM3-Audio #65826, #65827, #65828

Ming3-ASR #63585
NVIDIA Parakeet TDT Through the vllm-parakeet-plugin #65005

Highlights

Extensible KV cache, on by default

  • On CUDA and ROCm, the KV cache is sized from memory actually free after CUDA graph capture and warmup, not from an estimate (#56492).
  • Result: a larger cache (e.g. MiniMax-M3 on H200: 433k → 672k tokens), so throughput is higher and TTFT lower at high concurrency.
  • Trade-off: per-token decode latency can rise on some models (TPOT +6–18% on some H200 models at concurrency 128). Opt out with --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 or --no-enable-extensible-kv-cache.
  • Hardened with fixes for allocator fragmentation, startup OOMs and KV connectors (#67296, #67485, #66731, #66523, #66197, #65137, #66605, #66674).

Model Runner V2 only

  • Model Runner V1 is removed (#63373).
  • Dual-batch overlap now runs on MRV2, including with speculative decoding and DCP (#61464).

Speculative decoding

  • Suffix decoding runs on MRV2 with a GPU speculator; Arctic Inference is no longer needed (#60339).
  • Custom speculators: declarative configs plus a register_speculative_method plugin API (#63205).
  • CUDA graphs for MRV2 draft-model speculators (#60989).
  • Adaptive verification works with XPress (#65175).
  • Draft KV cache matches the target's dtype, so an FP8 target gets an FP8 draft cache (#65198).

Performance

Improvement Hardware Gain PR

KV-balanced MLA decode for Kimi-K3 (opt-in) GB300 1.34–1.59× decode attention #63638
Qwen3.5 on breakable CUDA graphs (no torch.compile) NVIDIA 3.0–8.8% lower decode ITL #51012
FlyDSL decode monokernel, Muse Spark Open DSpark 8×MI355X +35–57% interactivity at conc. 1–8 #63440

AMD ROCm

  • Release images and wheels are ROCm 10.0 only (#61939).
  • MoRI EPv2 via --all2all-backend mori (#61361).
  • Kimi-K3 specialized decode on MI355X, opt-in (#61435).
  • TRITON_ATTN is the default attention backend on RDNA3 and RDNA4 (#60418).

Serving and operations

  • Checkpoint/restore (CRIU + cuda-checkpoint) through /checkpoint/prepare, /checkpoint/status and /checkpoint/restore, in both the Python and Rust frontends (#62570).
  • Fault-tolerant DP+EP scale-down: dead ranks are removed and their experts redistributed without a restart (#46370).
  • Best-effort NUMA binding on by default (#61258).
  • Opt-in cache-aware admission ordering (#54625).
  • Rust frontend: stateless Responses API (#63902) and n > 1 (#65625).

Running one coding agent is easy; running ten that share GitHub, Linear and CI turns software delivery into a distributed systems problem. James Moss, Member of Technical Staff at Tessl, shares five lessons from scaling Tessl's own software factory to 3.5x more merged PRs with the same team: shared state, stale assumptions, convergence, duplicate work, and budgets with stop conditions. – How Tessl's internal software factory grew to handle 85% of PRs
– Why independent tickets don't guarantee independent changes
– Catching stale assumptions when other agents change the code underneath
– Stopping review agents from talking in circles
– Idempotency and fault tolerance for factories built on third-party tools
– Budgets and stop conditions for multi-agent workflows

items.title: CrossEnv: Synthesizing Verifiable Cross-Environment Tasks for Long-Horizon Agent Training
items.summary: Executable synthetic environments provide scalable training tasks and verifiable feedback for long-horizon agents. Existing environment synthesis methods primarily generate tasks within individual environments. However, these tasks do not adequately capture real-world interactions across services, where actions in one service depend on information obtained from another. Synthesizing such tasks is challenging because data generated across environments must remain consistent to support executable and verifiable interactions. To address this challenge, we introduce CrossEnv, a framework that uses an entity-tool graph to identify connections between environments and aligns task-specific data to synthesize executable, verifiable cross-environment tasks. We further propose CrossEnv-Curriculum, which progresses from single-environment tool use to coordination across more environments and business domains, before introducing user interaction. Across four external benchmarks, combining cross-environment training data with this curriculum achieves competitive performance with fewer training examples. Further analyses support the benefits of cross-environment data and curriculum training, and provide evidence of transfer to new environment combinations, external tasks less similar to the training data, and longer workflows.

items.title: StitchRAG: Constructing Compact and Evidence-Preserving Contexts for RAG with Diffusion-Based Stitching
items.summary: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) improves factuality by grounding large language models (LLMs) in external evidence. However, long retrieved contexts incur computational overhead and can even hurt performance due to noisy or irrelevant content. We propose \textsc{StitchRAG}, a framework for constructing compact context in RAG. \textsc{StitchRAG} builds a faithful, information-dense context while dynamically compressing the retrieved passages. We adapt the size reduction ratio to each passage by formulating a utility maximization trading-off the retained information and computation costs. We then extract answer candidates and query-related keywords from passages as anchors and collect passage sentences containing anchors under the derived size constraint. Finally, we connect or stitch the collected sentences together using text diffusion to form a coherent and natural context. Experiments on five open-domain QA benchmarks show that \textsc{StitchRAG} consistently outperforms diverse multi-step and compression baselines. Extensive ablations show the effectiveness of dynamic size allocation, anchor preservation, and diffusion-based stitching.

The gains come from building on what is new in Rubin: kernels tuned for its split memory and FP4 tensor cores, specialized decode kernels for low latency, and a rack-wide KV cache and Engram tables shared over NVLink. This is the third post in our DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash series. The first post covered day-0 bring-up and kernel fusions. The second scaled the model to a GB300 NVL72 rack with P/D disaggregation and Wide-EP. This post moves the same stack to Vera Rubin NVL72, which we introduced last month . Rubin opens up new avenues for optimization. We start with the hardware facts that shaped our work, then go through four groups of optimizations: Figure 1: SemiAnalysis AgentX on NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 (vLLM, P/D disaggregation, Wide-EP) vs. GB300 NVL72. Throughput counts cached input, uncached input and output tokens ( GB300 source ). We measure performance with the SemiAnalysis AgentX benchmark as a representative agentic serving workload, aligned with our previous posts. Figure 1 compares the two racks' raw throughput (total tokens per GPU per second, including input, cached, and output) and power-normalized throughput, respectively in two tabs. items.title: claude-code v2.1.326
items.summary:
What's changed

  • Added support for turning on Code Mode while agent teams are enabled; if you already turned it on, sessions with teams on now start in Code Mode
  • Added a startup warning when an --allowedTools, --disallowedTools or --tools value has an entry that doesn't look like a complete rule
  • Added a message explaining why MCP servers stop loading when an administrator adds managed-mcp.json during a session
  • Added a row to /status that says when your provider or an environment variable such as DISABLE_TELEMETRY turns features off
  • Added a note in /plugin and claude plugin list when a malformed plugin.json field such as author or homepage is ignored
  • Added Ctrl+O to show hidden startup notices
  • Added a hint in the empty prompt that says what to do after a request fails
  • Added an esc to stop footer hint in a subagent's view where Esc would stop it
  • Added OTEL_RESOURCE_INCLUDE_HOST to include host.name and host.id in OpenTelemetry resource attributes (off by default)
  • Added overflowX="scroll" on a mod's Box, and maxLines and wrap="clip" on its Text
  • Fixed cp of a file being refused when only its source was covered by an Edit deny rule
  • Fixed Bash commands that delete or overwrite files (find -delete, cat a > b, sort -o) being summed up in the transcript as a search or a read
  • Fixed a misleading "Dangerous rm operation" warning in the Bash permission prompt on some commands with no rm that Claude Code can't read reliably
  • Fixed background sessions losing the LLM gateway your shell exported after a crash, after a reopen from another folder, or when the background service lacks it: they now stop before any model request
  • Fixed the background service ending your own processes, such as an SSH login, when a process number on its list had been reused by another user's process
  • Fixed rules added in /permissions or at a main-conversation tool prompt, and /add-dir folders, looking saved when the settings file couldn't be written; the terminal now warns and names it
  • Fixed a failed MCP headersHelper, or one not run in an untrusted folder, making other sessions start without that server, for most servers with no stored OAuth refresh token
  • Fixed managed settings with certain key names stopping Claude Code from starting or affecting other managed files
  • Fixed settings files with values nested thousands of levels deep crashing Claude Code or applying only some of the time; values past 64 levels are now dropped with a warning
  • Fixed a settings file saved with an error mid-session being skipped silently; a warning now names the file
  • Fixed the subagent model set in managed settings not applying in Claude Desktop's Code tab; it now overrides your own, as in a terminal, unless those settings also pick a provider or gateway
  • Fixed sandboxed commands failing to start on Linux when the home or config directory is reached through a symlink into /net and sandbox settings deny reads of it
  • Fixed empty placeholder files, including .git/config.lock, sometimes being left in the project on Linux when Claude Code was stopped during a sandboxed command
  • Fixed Up then Enter answering Yes at the folder trust prompt shown under an already trusted parent folder
  • Fixed an extra Enter at the end of setup accepting the offer to make auto mode the default
  • Fixed a message typed over the startup auto mode offer being lost, and its Enter accepting the offer
  • Fixed a note typed on a permission prompt being sent to Claude after Tab had hidden it
  • Fixed PreToolUse hooks in managed settings leaving no OpenTelemetry tool_decision event or permission_denials entry when they refused a direct tool call
  • Fixed letters typed over /sandbox or a delete question in /permissions moving the selection
  • Fixed resumed sessions losing recent turns after a crash when the previous turn ended with an empty reply
  • Fixed resumed sessions losing earlier conversation history when Claude Code ran low on memory
  • Fixed a re-sent file overwriting Claude's changed copy in Remote Control and cloud sessions on Linux with no feature flags loaded: the copy moves to a .kept- folder, or the new file isn't saved
  • Fixed a background session being killed and its request lost when you opened, stopped or removed the older session whose conversation it had resumed
  • Fixed claude purge hiding its prompts when stdout is redirected, where one unseen Enter could delete a project's data; they now show on the terminal
  • Fixed the spend limit menu removing the monthly limit without asking when Backspace and Enter were pressed as it opened
  • Fixed /rewind restoring only some files after running /branch twice while a slow backup copy was still running
  • Fixed /rewind saying "No code changes" when a shell command changed files it can't restore; a turn whose changes weren't tracked now reads "Code changes unknown"
  • Fixed /rewind: Esc now cancels its summary, its list shows more than one past prompt in fullscreen, and a long prompt no longer hides its warning about losing later file changes
  • Fixed Ctrl+C or Ctrl+D twice in /skills quitting Claude Code and dropping changes; it now saves and closes the panel
  • Fixed the usage limit menu erasing your draft and opening while you were typing
  • Fixed pasted text and images being dropped when ↑ recalls a draft cleared with Esc Esc
  • Fixed an edited typed answer to Claude's question sending the old text when you moved on without pressing Enter
  • Fixed going back to a question you answered from its list putting the cursor on the first option, where Enter replaced your answer
  • Fixed /feedback and /bug sending the report when you typed a space on the confirmation screen, and losing the typed report after Ctrl+O or Ctrl+Z
  • Fixed a prompt typed after --add-dir, --allowedTools or another list option being dropped without a message
  • Fixed /plan <description> ignoring the description when plan mode was already on
  • Fixed valid PDFs being dropped from the conversation after the API rejected a different PDF read in the same batch
  • Fixed a session ending after a single failed memory allocation while drawing the screen
  • Fixed compaction on Bedrock, Vertex and Foundry, and with telemetry turned off, sometimes replying to one of your messages instead of summarizing, or leaving Claude's last reply out of the summary

  • Changed auto mode to ignore some wildcard shell allow rules, such as ones that name no program or that start with $HOME, so the safety check decides those commands
  • Changed auto mode to judge wildcard allow rules whose program is a Windows backslash path, so those calls can be blocked; exact rules keep their allow; we plan to restore rules that start with .\
  • Changed a managed autoMode.environment list without "$defaults" to replace every built-in entry in Claude Desktop and Agent SDK apps too; add "$defaults" or copy the sensitive-target ones
  • Changed --add-dir and /add-dir in local terminal sessions to show the trust prompt for a folder you have not trusted yet; claude --bg refuses such a folder
  • Changed self-hosted runners under --trust-workspace false to ignore more repository settings; set such values in user or managed settings
  • Changed how permission answers over Remote Control and on self-hosted runners save "always allow" choices
  • Changed enabled plugins that were refused for a malformed plugin.json display field: they now load, with their hooks and MCP servers; administrators should check the plugins they deploy
  • Changed how allowedHttpHookUrls and httpHookAllowedEnvVars apply to hooks from managed settings
  • Changed HTTP hooks to ignore Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding in their headers setting; the request's length comes from its body
  • Changed plugin uninstall to also delete the files extracted from the plugin's MCP bundles (.mcpb, .dxt), unless another plugin uses the same bundle
  • Changed some worktree sessions to skip some plugin settings; a notice names what was skipped
  • Changed /plugin uninstall, remove and switch questions to lists answered with the arrow keys and Enter, or Esc to cancel; y, n and u no longer answer them
  • Changed automatic compaction in plan mode to use the model answering you, such as Opus with opusplan, so it can cost more
  • Changed Cowork cloud sessions to hold an organization's OpenTelemetry export until the first turn; a session that gets no message now sends nothing, so claude_code.session.count can fall
  • Changed Claude's messages to a session on another machine to be refused when your session uses an API key, auth token, profile or workload identity beside a saved claude.ai login
  • Changed --bare sessions on an unapproved API key: moving one to the background is now refused in most setups, and claude --bare --bg exits with an error if the background service lacks the key
  • Changed "Continue automatically at usage limit" to stop with a notice, sending nothing, when your login changes or ends during the wait
  • Remote Control: Changed how it connects through a proxy: requests now use a CONNECT tunnel, so a proxy that refuses CONNECT stops Remote Control with an error
  • Remote Control: Changed the session debug logs written under --verbose to go to ~/.claude/child-logs/
  • Self-hosted runner: Changed Linux and macOS sessions with no gh to get a built-in gh api by default, via Anthropic, which adds their GitHub sign-in, if any; --use-anthropic-gh false turns it off
  • Changed agent view so that quitting with Ctrl+C twice, Ctrl+D twice or /exit after pressing ← in an empty conversation ends that session, instead of leaving it running for 5 minutes
  • Changed --await-initialize to be refused with --bg or --worktree --tmux, which never read the initialize request, instead of starting without the fields it carries
  • Changed worktree creation, /teleport and IDE checkouts to run git with a stricter PATH; a git filter or helper may need its full path
  • Changed the card for approving a subagent's plan to two choices, "Yes, and switch to default (ask each time) for this session" and "No", chosen with the arrow keys and Enter (typed text moves to No)
  • Changed the /claude-api skill to build agents on Managed Agents by default, unless you want to host the agent loop yourself
  • Changed /usage in fullscreen mode to show plan limit bars before session cost for subscribers; /cost still starts with cost
  • Changed the wording of some messages that claude subcommands print; JSON output is unchanged
  • Changed first-run setup to preselect the "Auto (match terminal)" theme instead of Dark mode
  • Changed fullscreen /cd to refuse "Yes" while its trust prompt doesn't fit, with a line saying to make the window taller
  • Removed the tmux notice that said the mouse wheel needs set -g mouse on in fullscreen; the wheel scrolls without it
  • Removed the spinner tip that suggested /clear 30 minutes into a running turn
  • [VSCode] Added a claudeCode.promptSuggestions setting that turns prompt suggestions off
  • [VSCode] Fixed "Rewind code to here" in a forked conversation sometimes undoing one turn too many and deleting files created in that turn
  • [VSCode] Fixed the Sandbox dialog creating empty files and folders in the home directory and the project's .git folder while the sandbox is off
  • [VSCode] Fixed the saved sign-in being lost on some networks
  • [VSCode] Fixed sign-in ending when a verification code, a web address or a code from another sign-in attempt is pasted; the panel now says what to paste instead
  • [VSCode] Fixed the sign-in screen showing briefly each time a panel or window opened while signed in to Console without an API key
  • [VSCode] Fixed the usage-limit banner's "Request more" button for Team and Enterprise members coming back after each press without sending anything, after you signed in again during a session
  • [VSCode] Fixed /ide in a second Claude Code session silently losing the editor connection back to the first session; the newest connection now wins and the displaced session shows how to switch back
  • [VSCode] Fixed saved memories not being listed in the Memory dialog, or RAM use growing without end, when the memory folder held symlink loops, and a hang when it held a named pipe
  • [VSCode] Fixed a running command's live output stopping after one failed read
  • [VSCode] Fixed "Open in Terminal" showing only the shell's error when claude could not be started: in bash, zsh, fish and Git Bash, a notice now explains why and links to the install guide
  • [VSCode] Fixed the panel showing no "Open artifact" link after Claude publishes an artifact
  • [VSCode] Fixed the prompt suggestion hiding the "attach selected text" hint while the chat panel is unfocused
  • [VSCode] Fixed buttons with no visible border in the high-contrast themes, and the dark welcome art on the sign-in screen in Light High Contrast
  • [VSCode] Improved Edit and Write speed: no wait for new problems on files that are not open in a tab when the editor has been reporting none for such files
  • [VSCode] Changed a running command's live output in the chat to look like the command card's OUT row
  • [VSCode] Changed the text of extension errors in event listeners, views and activation to stay out of the editor's own error telemetry

items.title: aws-emulator
items.summary:
aws-emulator

Finally, an official emulator from AWS to run tests against a local clone of their many different services without having to provision a paid API key to do so.

It's written in Rust by a huge swarm of agents - 29,684 commits in the first three weeks of the project. Swaminathan (Swami) Sivasubramanian wrote about how it came to be in a guest post on Werner Vogels' blog.

It currently requires Docker to run on macOS or Windows. I'm hoping they fix that in the future - it would be great if you could download a single binary and use that as part of a standard test suite in other languages and on other platforms.

items.title: Why PMs are suddenly valuable again | Tulsee Doshi (Head of Product, Gemini)
items.summary:
Tulsee Doshi is head of product for Google’s frontier AI models, including Gemini and other multimodal models, such as Nano Banana, Genie, Veo, and Lyria.

*We discuss:*
1. Why model development is not just engineering, but also like Snape’s potions class
2. Google’s full-stack frontier AI strategy
3. What PMs do inside a frontier AI lab
4. Tulsee’s 60-20-20 framework for balancing what works now and what’s almost working
5. How to write your first eval
6. The rising value of great PMs

*Brought to you by:*

(42:38) Google’s opportunity to build a personal AI assistant
